• The shop restocks by buying at the local public market (palengke) about every two weeks, with small top-ups in
between. There are no suppliers, purchase orders or delivery lead times: the shopping list is the plan and the
• The shopping list is a fixed rule over the last 28 days of sales and waste, not a forecast: usage per day × the
days to cover (until the next trip, or fewer if it won't stay fresh) + safety stock, never above par, minus
what's on hand, rounded up to market units.
• Recording a purchase is the owner's (Administrator's) work, since it carries prices. The price paid becomes the
item's cost per unit, so recipe costs, margins and food cost follow the market. Freshness assumes the oldest
stock is used first; stock is one number per item, not batches.
